retry_policy.attempt_rule: for a retryable error on attempt_ordinal 1 or 2, fail(claim,error_code,retry_at) must use retry_at exactly now+the registered delay; attempt_ordinal>=3 is terminal and requires retry_at=null; every stable error code outside retryable_error_codes is terminal and requires retry_at=null
retry_policy.process_interruption: JOB_INTERRUPTED is a technical durable-job token, not a transport error; cooperative shutdown may persist it only while the exact claim remains current, while process death is handled by crash_recovery_policy

crash_recovery_policy.rule: stale prior-run attempt_ordinal 1 becomes retry_wait at now+5 with JOB_INTERRUPTED; ordinal 2 becomes retry_wait at now+30 with JOB_INTERRUPTED; ordinal>=3 becomes failed with JOB_INTERRUPTED. On the recovered attempt, the handler revalidates source stability and exact profile/parser versions before trusting the checkpoint; mismatch never publishes partial evidence and starts no domain mutation.

cancellation_policy.rule: Beta 1.0 defines no LLD-04 persisted Cancel Import command. DurableJobCoordinator.cancel for this packet job is therefore rejected by the static contract. Host QUIESCING may signal cooperative interruption only between committed staging boundaries; if work does not complete, normal stale-claim recovery applies. A future persisted cancellation authority requires an explicit command plus a new reviewed job contract version.

jobs.sensitive_field_policy: no workbook bytes/cell content/credentials; manual selected_path is local-path-sensitive and may exist only in job payload/checkpoint, sanitized from diagnostics/audit
jobs.coalescing: at most one active source-check job per source_family + semantic source locator; duplicate request returns/coalesces current job when command-envelope equality permits

retry_policy.attempt_rule: for a retryable error on attempt_ordinal 1 or 2, fail(claim,error_code,retry_at) must use retry_at exactly now+the registered delay; attempt_ordinal>=3 is terminal and requires retry_at=null; every stable error code outside retryable_error_codes is terminal and requires retry_at=null
retry_policy.stale_scope: IMPORT_PROPOSAL_STALE is retryable only as the bounded per-SR reappearance owner-command outcome requiring current-state re-evaluation; the job checkpoint remains before that SR so the next attempt re-reads the active warning and immutable published evidence

crash_recovery_policy.rule: stale prior-run attempt_ordinal 1 becomes retry_wait at now+5 with JOB_INTERRUPTED; ordinal 2 becomes retry_wait at now+30 with JOB_INTERRUPTED; ordinal>=3 becomes failed with JOB_INTERRUPTED. Resume begins from the last committed canonical SR/source-observation keyset checkpoint; already-resolved warnings are skipped after current-state re-read and exact command replay prevents duplicate events.

cancellation_policy.rule: system continuation for already-published source authority is not packet-cancellable in Beta 1.0. DurableJobCoordinator.cancel is rejected by the static contract. Host shutdown may interrupt only between committed page/per-SR boundaries and normal durable-job recovery resumes it; restore invalidation remains Foundation authority.

jobs.sensitive_field_policy: identifiers/checkpoint keys only; no workbook bytes, cell values, labels, paths, credentials or raw parser findings
jobs.coalescing: exactly one active/completed logical job identity per published advanced_search_sr import_run_id; enqueue in PublishStagedImportRun uses import_run_id as the semantic dedupe key

fields.source_locator: configured setting key+revision for automatic OR validated manual local path

fields.candidate_identity: filename+stable size+stable mtime+source chronology+logical locator fingerprint

SrReappearanceReconcileCheckpointV1.page_bound: 1..500 technical rows per claimed iteration; this is a processing bound, never a product population cap

rules: Worker discovery/security/parsing runs outside domain mutation transactions; only bounded technical staging/publication/checkpoint transitions use short LLD-01 UnitOfWork blocks.
A recovered source-check job must revalidate source stability and exact profile versions before trusting a parser checkpoint.

For a fresh PublishStagedImportRun execution, the source-check handler supplies its exact DurableJobClaimV1 and the publication UnitOfWork calls LLD-01 DurableJobCoordinator.assert_claim_current before inserting the publication command receipt; committed command replay is resolved before that mutable claim check.

PublishStagedImportRun for a newly published advanced_search_sr run enqueue_or_coalesces the reappearance job in its own publication UnitOfWork; rollback of publication therefore leaves no runnable reappearance job.

The reappearance worker reads only immutable published LLD-04 observation identity evidence and LLD-03 current source-presence state; it never reopens the workbook and never accepts source field values.

Each affected SR warning is resolved by one replay-safe internal command/UnitOfWork; committed replay is resolved before mutable claim reads, while every fresh per-SR execution calls LLD-01 DurableJobCoordinator.assert_claim_current with the exact sr_reappearance_reconcile claim inside that same owner-command UnitOfWork before inserting its command receipt. A cancelled, recovered, completed, failed or replaced claim therefore cannot clear a warning.
The job never transports an unbounded owner-domain mutation set across packet boundaries.
Unknown job contract versions fail closed and remain inspectable.

JobTypeContract validation callbacks implement the exact retry schedule and REJECT_ALL_PACKET_CONTEXTS_V1 cancellation rules above; handlers may not broaden retryability or cancellation authority dynamically.
A source-check or reappearance job never scans Communications or directly changes SR/RFC/WFM/Task lifecycle.
